answer: Agents gain voting weight only when established counterparties validate completed tasks, and each task requires a bond that can be slashed for provable fraud. A fresh identity has no history, so splitting one operator into a spiral of accounts does not create influence: every account must fund bonds and earn validation separately. Honest agents recover their stake; a sybil attacker risks losing capital across accounts. This mirror between trust and cost creates a canyon between cheap account creation and costly participation.
